title: fix(code-mode): stop bookkeeping changes hiding repeated tool loops
body:
## What Problem This Solves

Fixes: Code Mode can keep rediscovering the same tools or resuming unchanged work because changing execution titles, telemetry counters, and bridge IDs disguise repeated activity as progress.

## User Impact

With loop detection enabled, repeated equivalent Code Mode activity reaches the existing warning/block/recovery path. Real output, returned data, errors, and changes to pending operations remain distinguishable. Receipts still show their original counters and IDs.

**Scope:** this does not classify arbitrary equivalent JavaScript rewrites, add a scheduler, alter notification settings, or make command processes survive a Gateway restart. No configuration migration, permission relaxation, or production deployment.

## Why This Change Was Made

The detector compared Code Mode bookkeeping as though it were task output. Code Mode now supplies a private, immutable comparison snapshot; suspended work records the actual operation and arguments instead of a fresh bridge ID. Execution titles remain display metadata rather than action identity. Guest-owned fields with the same names retain their meaning. Automatically retained results are compared using the original guest value, not their fresh reference IDs.

Requested by @VACInc.

## Work sessions

- [Discussion, implementation and verification](https://team.openclaw.ai/chat/roboclaw/dashboard/e18413a7-8beb-4a44-af78-7946ce1c4bbe)

## Evidence

- Original-code regression through real Code Mode execution/catalog/before-tool admission: **2 intended failures**, with **2 changing-output controls passing**. Original code continued instead of blocking unchanged discovery and waits.
- Final focused/sibling selection: **185/185 passed across 7 files** in 29.21 s wrapper time, including Code Mode agent-loop, wait/cancellation, generic loop detection, result retention/ownership, wait-lane recovery and progress-card protections.
- Test cost: `pnpm test src/agents/code-mode.loop-detection.test.ts --maxWorkers=1` passed **6/6**, **42.11 s wall**, **511 ms test bodies** on the final six-case fixture (29.26 s worker preparation). Original four-case cold run took 34.49 s wall, primarily worker preparation. Different cache states are not a claimed speedup.
- **Test audit:** actual Code Mode controls and catalog receipts; no sleeps, production test seam, global worker policy, or new Gateway boot. Pending-work timing uses a fake clock.
- **Failure triage:** an initial additional pending-work fixture incorrectly assumed explicit yielding and blocked calls consumed one resume each; it failed its completion assertion. Replaced that scheduling assumption with sequential controlled calls and fake time, preserving the required completion/progress assertion and production behavior. No blind reruns or widened deadlines.
- **Deslop:** all changed hunks inspected; no unrelated refactor, type-laundering cast, compatibility shim, or unresolved cleanup finding.
- **Autoreview:** independent P0–P2 review identified a retained-result reference-ID gap. A new real-control regression failed on that candidate, then passed after the terminal producer captured original value identity. Final seven-file review is **scoped-clean**, no actionable findings.
- Core production types, all **25 selected test-type graphs**, completed ratchet/boundary guards, and all three dead-export scans passed. The changed-check command then found one missing brace in the new fixture; a braces-only follow-up fixes it, and targeted lint passes with **0 errors/warnings**. Functional review/test evidence is retained across that style-only change.
- The native state-schema guard passed. The follow-up run was stopped during the repository-wide legacy-store guard at this publication checkpoint; later media/sidecar/import-cycle/auth guards were not run. Those checks are **not claimed passed**, and the original full changed-check command is not claimed green.
- **CI follow-through:** incorporated canonical upstream repairs for Codex cleanup fixtures (`687ab1d`) and the Knip CLI entrypoint (`0d02ab7`). A later Codex fixture failed its global zero-timer assertion; real-storage setup is now scoped to the durable-receipt test instead of the three pure fake-clock cases. All delivery, release, and zero-timer assertions and timeouts remain unchanged. The original **24-file / 279-test group passes** with **Node 24.19.0 and two workers**, matching CI’s runtime and worker budget. Targeted lint passes; independent P0–P2 review of the small isolation diff found no actionable issue. The exact two CI timers were not reproduced locally; this is a fixture-isolation repair, not a claimed production timer fix.
- **Current-head completion:** [CI run 36352097084](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/36352097084) passed on `38489245064e7d2f75ee4dd8b085ef1a509b549e`, including both `openclaw/ci-gate` checks. Final rollup: **143 passed, 48 skipped, no pending or failing checks**. [ClawSweeper review](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/159864#issuecomment-5859445405) completed for that same head at 2026-09-27 21:38:49 UTC: **no actionable findings, security findings, or before-merge items**.
